corrected_value.authors: Daou, M., Lohse, K. R., & Miller, M. W.
corrected_value.title: Expecting to teach enhances motor learning and information processing during practice

decisions.quote: The primary purpose of this research was to replicate the findings of Daou and colleagues (Daou, Lohse, et al., 2016; Daou, Buchanan, et al., 2016) Replications have been dichotomized into direct and conceptual categories (Makel et al., 2012) . According to Makel et al. (2012) direct replications seek to duplicate the original methods as closely as possible, whereas conceptual replications follow similar methods, but researchers purposefully modify features of the experimental protocol to test the rigor of the underlying hypotheses. Within this dichotomy, the approach adopted here aligned more with that of a direct replication. That is, we adopted the methods of the original experiment which first showed the effect (Daou, Buchanan, et al., 2016) , with the exception of including the more valid and reliable motivation and pressure measures that were used in their second experiment (Daou, Lohse, et al., 2016) .
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. The paper reports a preregistered replication (N = 76) explicitly retesting the golf-putting motor learning (retention radial error) and declarative free-recall advantages of expecting to teach reported across the first two experiments by Daou and colleagues: Daou, Buchanan, Lindsey, Lohse, & Miller (2016; Journal of Motor Learning and Development, 4(2), 197-207, DOI 10.1123/jmld.2015-0036) and Daou, Lohse, & Miller (2016; Human Movement Science, 49, 336-345, DOI 10.1016/j.humov.2016.08.009). In the Results and Discussion (including the TOST equivalence test against both original effect sizes, g = 1.08 and g = 0.82, and Table 6 comparing acquisition blocks across both studies), the authors directly evaluate and compare their data against both experiments. Shipped row 1065 covers only the first experiment (Daou, Buchanan, et al., 2016, DOI 10.1123/jmld.2015-0036); Daou, Lohse, & Miller (2016, DOI 10.1016/j.humov.2016.08.009) is a separate experiment with an independent sample, distinct acquisition and retention statistics, and additional IMI and motor preparation measures, so report equivalence does not apply.
